cases.summary: CompatBench smoke run (PR gate, fidelity forced): 24/24 cases pass all nine stages with 0 product bugs. Separate probe on final exports: the RenderCore canvas leg is pixel-identical to native on 5/5 figures. The worker re-serialization leg differs on 2 of 5; a control run traces one fully to the declared pdf.fonttype=42, and the other (art_colorbar, 0.39% pixels changed, limit 0.4%) has an unverified cause.
cases.audit_note: All 3 commands reproduced: exit codes 0/1/0; smoke 24/24 full_support; per-figure numbers identical (art_colorbar A leg 0.004337, 0.003908 after the fonttype42 control). Downgraded for two reasons. First, the B leg places the native PDF copy on the canvas with zero overrides and RenderCore embeds it as-is, so 5/5 zero pixel diff is guaranteed by construction; it does not show redraw fidelity. Second, on the one leg that actually redraws (A), art_colorbar still has 0.39% unexplained changed pixels after the fonttype42 control. That passes the threshold by only 0.0001, the threshold was borrowed from CompatBench's Agg-vs-Agg comparison, and the difference is not classified as the spec requires.

cases.summary: New test measures the data curve in the exported file: after appearance-only edits (color, line width, font size, legend position, figure size) every point stays in place, unit labels are kept, and script and data sha256 are unchanged even after write-back. Mutating line width to also change the data turns it red.
cases.audit_note: Counts match (2 / 107+1 skip / 1 passed). The executor's mutation reproduced (red, restored green). The ruler normalizes the curve into axes-fraction coordinates and deliberately skips tick values. My mutation (linewidth setter scales ydata by 1.1 and calls relim+autoscale_view) leaves the new test green (2 passed). An appearance patch that scales all data by 10% goes undetected, so the test does not meet the spec's criterion that raw/final arrays stay unchanged.

cases.summary: After a script structure change (reorder, insert before, delete A, insert a subplot), the override made for curve A lands on another curve in 4/4 variants, with no warning. Element IDs are position-based and nothing checks object identity.
cases.audit_note: Probe exit 1 / FAIL reproduced. Tried to find a reconciliation mechanism that would catch this and found none. The frontend OrphanOverrides check is also keyed on whether the gid exists; after A is deleted, beta takes over axes_0.lines_0. useServerEvents only shows a generic 'script changed' status. The fail stands.

cases.summary: Autosave behaves correctly under a real process kill before and after commit, disk-full and external conflict (plus 102 backend and 17 frontend tests pass). Write-back fails: disk-full while backing up the second target leaves the PDF replaced and the PNG old, leaves a .updating file, returns 500 and does not roll back.
cases.audit_note: Autosave probe PASS; write-back fault repro 2 failed (backup-ENOSPC: 500, changed ['Fig1.pdf'], leftover '.Fig1.png.updating'); 102 backend / 17 vitest pass. Reading app.py:4164-4175 confirms shutil.copy2 sits outside the try, so there is no cleanup and no rollback. The bug is real.

cases.summary: Existing 153 backend tests and 8 vitest tests pass. A new test reads the exported bytes with independent readers (PyMuPDF, Pillow, stdlib pdfread) and checks panel anchor, crop placement, page box, DPI and transparency. Mutating out the Y-axis flip turns it red.
cases.audit_note: 153 / 8 / 4 passed. Expected values come from an independent mm-to-px conversion, and the readers do not share code with the writer. The executor's y-not-flipped mutation reproduced (3 failed, restored green). The new test has a blind spot: the fixture square is symmetric in y (and in x under crop), so flipping flip_v (vertical mirror of the panel content) leaves it green. The same mutation turns 6 tests red in this case's own command set (test_export_endpoint) plus the rendercore tests, so pass holds at case level.

cases.summary: On a real worker, a deliberately slowed export of version A and a second edit exported as version B do not mix: each file has only its own title and revision. The §9 mutation (export the pre-edit version) turns 3 tests red, and the new tests pass 5 rounds in a row.
cases.audit_note: 2 passed; 5 stability rounds rc=0. The overrides=[] mutation reproduced (3 failed, restored green, tree clean). The subject is right: the export replays the overrides carried by the request and does not use the hot session's current state. It only compares title/data text, and the gate sits outside the worker lock; both limits fall within 'partial coverage'.

cases.summary: After the data file changes, a normal export keeps the edits and the old data, and the receipt says binding.matched=False. Only after /api/engine/invalidate does export use the new data, with edits reapplied. A mutation that makes export silently rerun the script turns it red.
cases.audit_note: 1 passed. Independent ground truth (the script writes the DATA text into the figure) plus binding.matched, with assertions in both directions. Mutation not redone (same shape and same file as the SCI-07 mutation, which was redone).

cases.audit_note: Reran every command and all counts match. Chromium 14/14, WebKit project 24/24, WebKit geometry flows 5/5. /Applications/Tavotto.app 0.16.0 fails both codesign --verify --deep --strict and spctl with exit 1. I re-downloaded the release tarball (af900af2…) and compared file by file: the main executable 7c730f1b… is identical, common files have zero content differences, the untouched release copy passes codesign, and the installed copy has exactly 17 extra engine/__pycache__/*.pyc files. The P1 repro exits 0 (system arm writes 16 .pyc, bundled arm writes 0). I redid the fix-style mutation (all three `child_args() if bundled else []` in pool.py replaced by `child_args()`): the repro stops reproducing, and after git checkout it reproduces again. Correction: the repro only explains 16 of the 17 files. The installed app's worker.cpython-313.pyc means some path imported engine.worker as a module, so a second writer is not yet located.

The nightly 35921334300 job results match. Correction: v0.16.0's support-matrix.json (at 4bf86c1f) has no macos-x86_64-desktop entry. That entry was added after the release, in 36a3025b (#539). So the missing darwin-x86_64 in latest.json is a newer promise being checked against the older release, not a v0.16.0 release defect. It should be treated as a precondition for the next release.
